newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-CRISTAL AIM TO MAKE LIBERTADORES HISTORY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CRISTAL AIM TO MAKE LIBERTADORES HISTORY.

text.p: Sporting Cristal could make Libertadores Cup history by becoming the first team from Peru to win the competition when they take on Cruzeiro of Brazil in the second leg of the final on Wednesday.
Cristal, who have knocked out two Argentine teams on their way to the final, will need to play above themselves after being held to a 0-0 draw in last week's first leg in Lima.
The team's Uruguayan coach Sergio Mackarian acknowledged that Cristal's chances suffered a blow with their failure to make the most of home advantage last week.
But on Wednesday his team will be boosted by the return of Brazilian-born Peruvian international Julinho and Ghanaian midfielder Prince Amoaka, who both missed the first leg through suspension.
Mackarian also hopes that home advantage will force Cruzeiro to open up and abandon the ultra-defensive tactics they employed in Lima.
"They will be obliged to come out and attack and hopefully we can exploit the spaces," he said.
Cristal will also be encouraged by the fact that they were held 0-0 at home by Argentina's Velez Sarsfield but went on to win 1-0 in Buenos Aires in the second round.
The Peruvians have several players on the doubtful list, including Peruvian internationals Nolberto Solano and Jorge Soto.
Universitario, another Lima team, were the only previous Peruvian finalists in 1972 but were beaten by Argentina's Independiente, who hold the record for the most Libertadores titles.
Cruzeiro, who have had a huge slice of luck in the competition, were champions in 1976 and beaten finalists the following year.

The Brazilians, who have changed manager during the course of the tournament, lost their first three matches in the first round. But they were saved by the rules, which generously allow three teams from each first round group into the next round.
Cruzeiro then needed penalty shootouts to overcome Ecuador's Nacional in the second round and Chile's Colo Colo in the semifinals.
